the functional role of a single fixed positive charged residue in the intracellular pore of the CFTR Cl(-) channel can be "transplant" to another residue in a different TM region, and that increasing the number of positive charges in the inner vestibules of the pore from one to two causes a decrease in Cl(-) conductivity.

the functional role of one fixed positive charge in the intracellular side of the pore of the CFTR Cl(-) channel can be "transferred" to a residue that is located in a different TM domain, and that the functional effects of two fixed positive charges in that part of the pore are to cause a net decrease in Cl(-) transport.

the functional role of one positive charge (K) in the inner pore of CFTR can be "transferred" to a residue 20 A distant in a different TM domain (S1141) of the channel, and that increasing the number of positive charges in the pore vestibule from one to two has a net negative effect on overall Cl(-) conductivity.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the functional role of the positive charge in the pore of the Cl(-) conductive channel of CFTR is to facilitate the rapid permeation of Cl(-) through the channel.
the number of fixed positively charged residues within the pore of CFTR is a key factor in the regulation of Cl(-) transport by this ion channel.

the functional effects of the S1141 mutation can be attributed to the fact that this residue is located in the inner vestibular region of the pore, where it is functionally equivalent to K95, and where increasing the number of positive charges from one to two has a net negative effect on the overall function of CFTR as a Cl(-) channel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the number of fixed charges in the inner pore vestibule determines the rate of Cl(-) permeation and the extent of block by cytosol.
